study.focal_model: TIPS (Tiny Inference-time Policy for Scaling) on frozen LLaDA-8B-Instruct

training.compute_printed: 935 × 128 × 32 = 3,829,760 example-level decoder evaluations for training rollouts

main_sampler.description: TIPSfull: learned Bernoulli visibility policy (reveal/defer masked, retain/remask visible) on frozen LLaDA-8B-Instruct, single 1×256 canvas, greedy token proposals, fitted power-law visibility schedule with logit calibration, deterministic greedy finalization

credited_component.text: TIPS, ~600K-parameter policy learning unmasking and remasking around a frozen dLLM

design.other_detail: D15 other: the trained component is the visibility policy (decoder frozen), trained with binary cross-entropy warmup on reference-derived visibility targets, then GRPO (RLVR) on terminal correctness rewards.
design.inherited_from: LLaDA-8B-Instruct (D01, D02, D04, D05, D06); Jazbec et al. (2026) conditionally independent Bernoulli actions (D08)

census.F2_detail: Greedy (argmax) token proposals and greedy deterministic finalization; positions revealed or remasked by sampled Bernoulli actions of the learned policy on confidence features, calibrated to a fitted power-law schedule (gamma about 0.145). Proposal temperatures 0.1-1.0 only in App. B.4.5.

evidence.quote: On GSM8K and MATH-500 with LLaDA-8B-Instruct, the full-canvas and two-block TIPS variants achieve 58.46% and 57.97% micro-averaged accuracy at a budget of 32 decoder evaluations, exceeding the strongest baseline in our main comparison by 12.1 and 11.6 percentage points, respectively.

On GSM8K and MATH-500 with LLaDA-8B-Instruct, the full-canvas and two-block TIPS variants achieve 58.46% and 57.97% micro-averaged accuracy at a budget of 32 decoder evaluations, exceeding the strongest baseline in our main comparison by 12.1 and 11.6 percentage points, respectively.
Both variants are trained at a budget of 32 evaluations and remain competitive at higher budgets without retraining.

remain competitive at higher budgets without retraining. These results demonstrate that learning when to reveal and reconsider tokens can improve the accuracy–compute trade-off without updating the decoder backbone.
At most decoder NFE budgets, we surpass previous state-of-the-art methods in accuracy on GSM8K and MATH-500 by up to 13.25 percentage points, otherwise remaining competitive.
Masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate responses by predicting unresolved positions in parallel and exposing selected predictions as context
We focus on finite-step decoding with a pretrained masked diffusion language model (dLLM).
Masked diffusion language models expose an inference-time choice: which positions become visible after each denoising pass.
Each final controller has 628,739 trainable parameters; fixed buffers are excluded from this count.

We apply the LLaDA-trained TIPSfull policy to Dream-v0-Instruct-7B without retraining.

We introduce TIPS, an approximately 600K-parameter policy that learns both unmasking and remasking while keeping the dLLM backbone frozen.

Our evaluation centers on 256-token mathematical reasoning, and the supplementary transfer experiments use a single seed; longer generations and broader task coverage remain important tests of generality.
TIPS also uses a fixed decoding horizon rather than an adaptive stopping rule, preserving further revision but foregoing savings from early termination.
Decoder-call budgets also do not directly capture wall-clock cost.
We compare the complete supervised warmup–RLVR recipe with its supervised parent and a policy trained with RLVR alone.
For each method, we evaluate the performance at exponentially increasing budgets T ∈{4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256}.
All methods use the exact same setting except for block decomposition, in which we followed the settings found in the method’s original manuscripts.
A dLLM predicts a vocabulary distribution at every position and the reverse process samples a candidate token at each masked position:
These logits determine which positions are preferred while also allowing an external unmasking schedule to control how many positions become visible.
At masked positions, the action reveals the decoder’s proposal or leaves the position masked; at visible positions, it retains the current token or remasks it for subsequent regeneration.
We minimize the binary cross-entropy between the policy probabilities and the targets
Token proposals are greedy, whereas visibility actions are independent Bernoulli draws conditional on the policy probabilities.
We primarily measure the micro-averaged accuracy of each method reported across different decoder-call budgets.
We assume greedy decoding from here on out.
